observations.summary: Pin the properties the owner test misses (Q2 append to existing ACL, Q3 no final predicate, Q5 append before charge survive it): add existing-ACL cases (owner allow unchanged/accepted, inherited foreign allow unchanged/refused), a second prepare that does not append, and a one-capture budget that refuses before any write; add a Drop guard (the test leaked two scratch dirs under Q1/Q4) and drop the pre-emptive remove_dir_all on a nonce path. Before any caller.

append_owner_zero_allow is now a public unaccounted native write; prepare charges it with the borrowed descriptor_acl_capture_cost() (conservative: 131 edges, ~7.7 KB vs ~5 calls). Define a documented append cost and accounted/reserved wrappers like the capture, and keep the raw function crate-private. Before any caller.

The shape precondition fabricates CapturedAclState::Entries(0) for the private predicate; correct here (gate only, final decision on a real capture) but it reintroduces the idiom 450 removed from callers. A dedicated private_shape(kind, uid, metadata) helper removes it.
If the append succeeds and the second capture/predicate then fails, the zero-rights owner allow remains: harmless (non-granting, owner-neutral) and keeps retries idempotent (U2). Document it.

Carried from r3 and now production-relevant: the non-ENOENT fetch branch is verified by reading only (an injectable fetch seam would pin it); clearing errno before acl_get_fd_np remains optional hardening.
